papers.summary: BMuon changes Muon’s spectral geometry to encourage structured channel pruning. In a 1B-parameter LLaMA-style experiment, it retained its unpruned perplexity after 80% pruning, but its unpruned perplexity was worse than Muon’s.
papers.relevance: Directly tests whether training improves compressibility while preserving language-model quality, and exposes a significant quality tradeoff.

evidence.quote: On the unpruned models, Muon achieves lower perplexity ( 10.92 10.92 versus 12.84 12.84 for BMuon), but its performance degrades rapidly under pruning. In contrast, BMuon preserves its unpruned performance up to 80 % 80\\% pruning, reaching 12.86 12.86 with activation ranking and 12.85 12.85 with μ \\mu ranking.

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility

papers.summary: Monarch-Muon applies Muon to structured factors. At the 6.89B reference size, the reported peak memory fell from 68.87 to 52.94 GB versus dense Muon; fixed-structure quality comparisons also favored Monarch-Muon over Monarch-AdamW.
papers.relevance: Combines factorization, learned spectra, and measured quality–memory–speed tradeoffs across model sizes.

evidence.quote: Monarch–Muon achieves lower final validation loss than Monarch–AdamW in all four structured comparisons (Table 1 ).
At 6.89B, Monarch–Muon reduces the full-step time by 45% and peak memory by 23% relative to dense Muon.

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: PMRC keeps optimizer states in a gradient subspace and adds a residual-gradient correction. Its LLM pretraining comparison reports the lowest training and validation losses among the tested memory-efficient methods.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses the quality and optimizer-state-memory tradeoff in low-rank LLM pretraining.

evidence.quote: PMRC consistently achieves the lowest training and validation losses among memory-efficient methods.
PMRC also requires less optimizer-state memory than AdamW while achieving lower losses at every scale.

papers.title: Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon

papers.summary: The paper proves that trace-norm-regularized fine-tuning admits global minimizers with rank controlled by a frozen-feature bottleneck, without NTK linearization. Its stationary-point result for factorized LoRA requires a generic perturbation and does not rule out spurious local minima.
papers.relevance: Directly informs LoRA geometry, nuclear-norm regularization, and principled rank selection.

evidence.quote: we prove that the trace-norm-regularized problem has a global minimizer whose rank is controlled by d Φ d_{\\Phi}
This is a first-order exclusion theorem, not a no-spurious-local-minima theorem; Proposition 4.9 gives an explicit limitation.

papers.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape

papers.summary: ReGRA diagnoses ineffective singular components in a rank-16 LoRA update, then uses residual task gradients to initialize a complementary second-stage adapter within a fixed total rank.
papers.relevance: Connects singular-value structure to practical LoRA rank allocation and downstream performance.

evidence.quote: Without retraining, we evaluate rank- k k approximations formed by retaining the top k k singular components. As shown in Figure 1 , we find that k = 3 k=3 yields the best downstream performance, whereas retaining additional components degrades it.
Under the same total-rank budget, ReGRA consistently achieves stronger overall performance across the evaluated benchmarks and even reaches the performance of the double-rank model.

papers.title: ReGRA: Residual-Gradient Adaptation for Complementary Low-Rank Fine-Tuning

papers.summary: Studies generalization versus memorization with controlled noise, reporting that projection onto top Fisher eigenvectors separates general task performance from noisy-sample memorization.
papers.relevance: Covers the user’s question about the geometry of memorization under corrupted supervision.

evidence.quote: We show that projecting model weights onto the top Fisher eigenvectors decouples general task performance from noisy sample memorization

papers.title: Fisher information and the geometry of memorization in neural networks

papers.summary: Idea2Prior combines identity-aware discovery, candidate assessment, bounded document evidence, and joint ranking. Its reported Hit@5 advantage comes from a small historical comparison whose authors identify sampling and contamination limitations.
papers.relevance: Provides concrete design ideas and evaluation cautions for a handwritten research-digest retrieval harness.

evidence.quote: The central design separates inexpensive assessment of a broad candidate pool from a bounded examination of document evidence.
The 30 query cases include overlapping targets and a manually assembled distribution; the first ten items in each tier are not a random sample of all scientific literature.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

limitations: Code availability and reproducibility were not verified.
The supplied PMRC passages do not establish full-step throughput, and the supplied ReGRA passages do not quantify its extra calibration or training cost.
The Fisher study was selected from abstract evidence only; its experimental controls were not inspected.
The digest omits other strong candidates, notably Ori and DT-LoRA, because it is limited to seven papers.
